github_repo.label: GitHub repository
must_include: A public GitHub repository you own
At least 10 meaningful commits made over 3 or more days (not one bulk upload)
A README that explains what it does and how to run it
Code that clearly uses {skill} for a real feature

live_link.label: Live website
must_include: A live URL of something you built, linked to its GitHub repository proof
The site should use {skill} in a way a visitor can see

certificate.label: Certificate
must_include: A certificate issued to you by name, for a course or exam that covers {skill}
A verification link or credential ID from the issuer, so it can be checked

professional_license.label: Licence or registration
must_include: Your licence, registration or permit showing your name, number, issuing body and expiry date
It must be current (not expired)
Optional but recommended: a link to your entry on the issuing body's public register, so it can be fully verified

portfolio_link.label: Portfolio link
must_include: A public page of your work: a portfolio, published writing, a design profile or a case study
Your name on the page, so the work can be tied to you
Work that clearly shows {skill}

work_sample.label: Work sample
must_include: A document or image of real work you produced (a plan, report, design, lesson plan, spreadsheet export or photo of finished work)
Work that clearly shows {skill}
Remove confidential, client or patient details before uploading

publication.label: Publication
must_include: A DOI or a link to a paper, article, chapter or book
Your name must appear as an author
The work should show {skill}

reference_letter.label: Reference letter
must_include: A letter from a manager, supervisor, lecturer or client, ideally on their organisation's letterhead
It should say how you used {skill}, with an example
It counts as self-reported: we can't contact the writer, but employers can

experience_letter.label: Experience letter
must_include: A letter from an employer confirming your role, dates and duties
It should mention {skill} or the duties that used it
It counts as self-reported: we can't contact the employer, but employers can

referee_confirmation.label: Referee confirmation
must_include: A referee who worked with you and can speak to {skill}: a manager, supervisor, colleague or client
Their name, role, organisation and email address (a work email counts for more than a personal one)
The role, organisation and dates they can confirm
